title: Multi-Agent Trust Hierarchy Benchmark: Can Sub-Agents Correctly Resolve Conflicting Instructions from Multiple Orchestrators?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Tests a fundamental multi-agent safety property: authority resolution. Incorrect conflict resolution can be catastrophic. The finding directly informs multi-agent system design patterns.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: The experimental setup is conceptually simple: send conflicting instructions from two sources and observe behavior. Can be implemented with API calls and prompt engineering. Does not require heavy compute or complex infrastructure.

narrow_scope.reasoning: 30 scenarios is moderate. The scenarios can be templated (same structure, different content). If authority signals are pre-defined, the main work is running experiments and measuring consistency. Feasible if scoped down to 15 scenarios.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Novelty not assessed due to partial Wave 3 completion.
